Method of Attack: Distributed via phishing campaigns using PDF attachments that download Windows Script Files (WSF) to infect Windows devices
Reply-chain phishing emails using stolen email exchanges with malicious attachments or links
WSF files execute obfuscated PowerShell scripts to download DLLs and inject into legitimate Windows processes
Provides initial access to corporate networks by dropping additional payloads like Cobalt Strike, Brute Ratel, and other malware
Lateral movement through networks, data theft, and ransomware deployment in extortion attacks
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with PDF attachments containing malicious WSF files
Reply-chain phishing emails exploiting ongoing email conversations
Indicators of Compromise: PDF files named 'CancelationLetter-[number].pdf' containing malicious WSF download
WSF files executing PowerShell scripts to download DLLs
DLL injected into Windows wermgr.exe (Windows Error Manager) process
Use of URLs to download DLLs to %TEMP% folder
